instructions: The night before, or at least 6 hours ahead: zest the lime. That should be about 2 tsp. Mince 3 of the garlic cloves. In a large zip-top bag, combine 3 tbsp of the olive oil, the lime zest, the minced garlic, the 3/4 tsp ancho chili powder, 1/4 tsp coriander, 1/4 tsp oregano, 3/4 tsp of the salt, the 1/4 tsp pepper and 1 1/2 tsp honey. Squish the bag to mix it. Add the 1.25 lb chicken, rub the marinade into it through the bag, seal it and set the bag in a bowl in the fridge. Keep the zested lime in the fridge for the sauce.

Rinse the 1 cup quinoa in a fine sieve. Add it to a medium pot with 2 cups water and 1/4 tsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.

Meanwhile, make the green sauce. Cut the jalapeño open and scrape out the seeds into a small bowl. Roughly chop the jalapeño. Add it to a blender with 2/3 cup loosely packed cilantro leaves, the last garlic clove, the 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 3 tbsp sour cream, 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Squeeze the zested lime into the blender. That should be about 1 tbsp. Blend until the sauce is smooth and pale green. Transfer it to a small bowl, cover and keep it in the fridge.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the cucumbers into rounds. Drain the black beans in a sieve and rinse them.

Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Lift the chicken out of the bag, let the extra marinade drip off and lay the pieces in the pan in a single layer. Cook it in two batches if they don't all fit with room between them.

Leave the chicken alone for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is browned and lets go of the pan. Flip the pieces and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board.

Add 1 cup of the corn to the same pan over medium high. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until some of the kernels have browned in spots. Stand back a little. It can pop. Transfer the corn to a bowl.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then slice it into bite size pieces.
Divide the quinoa among 4 bowls or lunch containers. Top each one with the chicken, corn, black beans, tomatoes and cucumbers, and chop a little more cilantro over the top.
If you're packing them for lunch, spoon the green sauce into small separate containers and keep everything in the fridge for up to 4 days.
Serve with the green sauce spooned over, and the jalapeño seeds on the side for anyone who wants heat.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the chicken at least 6 hours or overnight, the night before.
method_notes: Both versions season chicken with chili, cumin or ancho and lime notes, cook it quickly in a hot pan or on the grill, slice it and pile it on quinoa with corn, tomatoes and other fresh toppings. Once Upon a Chef marinates tenderloins for at least 6 hours in olive oil, lime zest, garlic, ancho chili powder, coriander, oregano and honey, grills them for a few minutes a side and blends a creamy green sauce of jalapeño, cilantro, mayonnaise, sour cream and lime. Valentina's Corner seasons pounded breast just before cooking and browns the corn in the same pan with butter. This follows Once Upon a Chef for 4 in a skillet instead of a grill, with the corn browned in the chicken pan from Valentina's Corner and the sauce kept in its own container so the bowls pack well.
